# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 5 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 5 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_005_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 2, Chapter 1

**1** Here is the vision I received, my friends: **2** I had been fasting for many days, earnestly asking God to show me what he had promised through the elderly woman. Then one night she appeared to me and said: "You're so hungry to know and understand — come out early tomorrow morning to the field where you work, and I'll meet you there at the fifth hour and show you what you need to see." **3** "Which part of the field, my lady?" I asked. "Wherever you prefer," she said. I picked a quiet, pleasant spot. Before I could even describe the location to her, she said, "I'll find you wherever you go." **4** So I went out to the field the next morning, friends, counted off the hours, and arrived at the spot I'd chosen. There I found an ivory couch set out, with a linen cushion and a fine linen cover spread over it. **5** The place was completely empty — no one around at all. I was flooded with awe. A shaking came over me, my hair stood up. I was alone, and scared. Then I pulled myself together. Just then I saw the elderly woman walking toward me, carrying a small book. She sat down alone and said, "Hello, Hermas!" **6** I was too upset to smile. "Hello, my lady," I managed through tears. "Why so sad, Hermas?" she asked. "You're normally so patient and cheerful — what's happened?" "It's this fine woman who says I've sinned against her," I said. **7** "Nonsense," she replied. "A servant of God doesn't do such things! But yes, the thought did cross your heart — and it's exactly that kind of thought that opens the door to sin in God's servants. An evil, shameful intention like this is wrong in any righteous person. And in you, Hermas — someone known for self-control, for avoiding every evil desire, for simplicity and genuine innocence — it is even worse." **8** "But God isn't angry with you only because of that. He also wants your household to come to repentance, because they've been sinning against the Lord and against you, their own parents. You love your children — but you let things slide, and your household sank into serious trouble without correction. That's why God is displeased with you. But he will put everything right; he will undo all the past damage. The strain you've felt — that comes from carrying your family's sins. God's great mercy has seen you, and he will rebuild your family and restore your standing before his glory."

---

*PNEUMA note: The ivory couch with linen suggests a kind of heavenly prepared throne, emphasizing the dignity and deliberateness of the visionary encounter.*
